job.title: Principal Project Officer
job.description:
Resources Safety and Health Queensland (RSHQ) is the independent regulator of worker safety and health in Queensland's mining, quarrying, petroleum, gas and explosives industries. Their strategic plan focuses on protecting and promoting the safety and health of persons from risks associated with the resources industry. We are seeking a Principal Project Officer to support the Health Surveillance Unit.

As the Principal Project Officer, you will be responsible for the successful delivery of key projects and programs including free respiratory health checks for former mine and quarry workers across Queensland and their promotion to the community by overseeing contracts with service providers.

You will also provide support and advice in administering the Coal Mine Workers’ Health Scheme (Scheme), contribute to quality records management, and support business change in a fast paced, dynamic environment.

About you

It would be highly beneficial if you have knowledge, skills and experience in:

  • Oversee the effective administration of contracts with service providers, ensuring compliance with terms and conditions, resolving complex issues, and driving performance to achieve program objectives.
  • Implementation and oversight of quality assurance and continuous improvement frameworks to ensure service providers consistently deliver high quality services.
  • Conduct analysis of complex data and trends to identify systemic risks, evaluate provider performance, and measure program effectiveness.
  • Provide strategic recommendations and prepare reports to inform decision-making and drive continuous improvement to optimise service delivery.
  • Facilitate regular communication and positive relationships with service providers to monitor performance, address challenges and share feedback to improve service delivery.
  • Implement risk management strategies to maintain integrity of the program and adherence with legislative requirements.
  • Provide guidance and support to Senior Project Officer for the successful administration of program outcomes and objectives.
  • Liaise, negotiate and develop effective networks with internal and external stakeholders to deliver program objectives.
  • Apply standards, legislation, project management methodology, policies and procedures in a service delivery environment.
  • Lead the design, planning and execution of promotional activities that are driven by evidence and demonstrate sound financial awareness.

The role works closely alongside RSHQ's inspectorates and engages with a range of stakeholders across the resource sectors which may include workers, operators, industry and stakeholder representatives and medical practitioners, requiring excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills. The role directly provides benefit to the health of Queensland resource sector workers, which requires a highly dedicated and motivated officer to ensure this important value is delivered.

The successful candidate may be required to undergo any pre-employment checks including psychometric profiling, disciplinary history and criminal history that may be undertaken.

The role description will outline any qualifications, licences and specific requirements of the role. If you are interested in this job, we encourage you to read the attached role description and talk to the contact officer. 

How to apply

RSHQ, value the skills and insights we gain through a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the community we serve. RSHQ welcome and strongly encourage applications from people of all ages, life stages, caring responsibilities, intellectual/physical abilities, gender identity, sexual orientation, cultural background, and ethnicity to apply for positions with us.

Applications will remain current for twelve months and may be used to fill recurring vacancies during this time.

Your application should include the following elements:

  • A written statement (no more than 2 pages) outlining your suitability for the role.
  • A copy of your resume (no more than 4 pages).

The successful candidate may be required to undergo any pre-employment checks including disciplinary history and criminal history that may be undertaken.

For a confidential discussion please contact Ian Quinn on 0403 343 097.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button.

job.title: Assistant Treasurer
job.description:
This is a rare opportunity to join the global Head Office of a highly successful international business which is consistently regarded as an innovative and influential market leader in a highly competitive industry.

Reporting to the Group Treasurer, this high-profile position will lead the Treasury function across the business, ensuring the best outcomes for the Group on all treasury and corporate finance related activities.  As manager of the Treasury Front Office team, the Assistant Treasurer is responsible for financial market risk and funding for the Group, including developing financing plans and refinancing bank facilities and debt capital market transactions. The role is also responsible for capital management initiatives including financial modelling and the evaluation of debt capacities to inform the dividend strategy, and the execution of share buy-backs.  You will work closely with the Tax and Corporate Finance teams to manage internal capital management processes and the Corporate Development team to support strategic M&A transactions.  Interfacing with bank relationship managers, financial markets specialists, investment banks, ratings agencies and a range of internal stakeholders are also key elements of the role.

Technically and commercially strong, you will be operating at a senior level and have a background in a large corporate, consulting firm and/or financial services company. Previous experience and extensive knowledge of debt capital markets and financial risk management, combined with strong communication and relationship development skills are essential.

You are seeking an honest, candid and outcome focused culture and an opportunity to contribute significantly to the continued growth and success of this market leader, both domestically and globally.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Ian Hackett on 0408 312 216.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Analyst, Risk & Compliance
job.description:
Assemble is an end-to-end housing company which originates, delivers and manages sustainable, well-designed housing investment opportunities on behalf of institutional investor clients. By partnering across Government, industry and the community housing sector, Assemble delivers strong outcomes for investors while helping make housing more affordable and accessible for Australians. Assemble pursues this work with ambition, and holds itself accountable for delivering outcomes that are genuinely impactful for the communities it serves. As the organisation continues to grow, an opportunity has arisen for a risk and compliance professional to play a key role in the ongoing development and implementation of the Risk and Compliance Framework.

Reporting to the Deputy Company Secretary and Compliance Manager, this role takes ownership of the implementation and ongoing management of the Risk and Compliance Framework, working closely with business units to embed practical, risk-based approaches to compliance across the organisation. Key responsibilities include maintaining corporate and project risk registers, assisting with risk and compliance reporting for the Executive and Board, and supporting the governance team on statutory and Community Housing regulatory obligations. This broad role also contributes to company secretarial duties and assurance activities, and offers genuine scope to build and improve governance processes as Assemble continues to grow. This is a role for someone who takes ownership of outcomes and brings an authentic, solutions-focused approach to their work.

You will be a compliance and risk professional with approximately 3 to 5 years’ experience gained within a highly regulated industry, ideally within community housing or property development, although candidates from other regulated industries will also be considered. You will hold a tertiary qualification in business or a related discipline, together with postgraduate study in risk or compliance, or a genuine commitment to pursuing this. Strong communication skills, sound judgement, and the ability to build credibility and influence outcomes across all levels of the organisation are essential. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious governance professional who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and wants to make an impactful contribution to Assemble's continued growth.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.
